samples.summary: Viewer "drops the formatting group" test passes regardless of whether `readOnly` is forwarded to the toolbar
samples.evidence: `notes-toolbar.tsx:398` computes `canFormat = !readOnly && mode !== "view"`. A viewer-role render starts in `viewMode === "view"` (shared-notes-layout.tsx:49-51), so the formatting group and Undo/Redo are hidden by the *mode* alone. If the `readOnly={readOnly}` prop on `NotesToolbar` (shared-notes-layout.tsx:113) were dropped, this assertion would still pass. The companion test "can reach the markdown source through the view menu" (line 216) switches the viewer to `edit` — the one state where the `readOnly` wiring is observable — but asserts only `viewMode`, never that formatting/undo/keymap controls remain absent. So the diff's viewer-safety wiring has no assertion that can fail.

samples.summary: `canUndo()/canRedo()` assertions in the read-only test hold with or without the new guard
samples.evidence: `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false); expect(api.canRedo()).toBe(false);` are made on a freshly constructed `MemNoteStore('hello')` that has had no successful local edit, so `store.canUndo()`/`canRedo()` are already false. The new `canUndo: () => !readOnly && store.canUndo()` (editor.ts:661-663) is therefore not exercised — the test would pass identically against the old `() => store.canUndo()`. Covering it needs a store with history (e.g. spy `canUndo` to return true) on a read-only mount.

samples.summary: No test for the changed divider drag math (`track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`) or the widened/touch-enabled divider
samples.evidence: The diff changes drag ratio computation from `rect.width` to `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`, widens the divider 7px→25px and adds `touch-action: none`. `grep` over packages/notes/src finds no test referencing `note-divider`, `pointerdown`, `splitRatio` or `touchAction`; editor.test.ts covers view-mode switching but never a drag. A regression in this math (divider trailing the pointer, or the panes jumping) would ship undetected. jsdom cannot lay out, but `offsetWidth`/`getBoundingClientRect` can be stubbed and the resulting `editorEl.style.flex` asserted.

samples.summary: Non-persistence is asserted only for view mode, not for keymap or blame gutter
samples.evidence: The file docstring (lines 9-10) and the component docstring (shared-notes-layout.tsx:32-35) claim that *no* preference is written back. Only `wafflebase:notes:viewMode` is checked (line 186). The toolbar also exposes the keymap picker and the show-authors toggle, wired to bare `setKeymap`/`setShowAuthors` (lines 109-111); if either were later swapped for the persisting `writeKeymap`/`writeShowAuthors` from notes-settings, an anonymous share-link visitor would silently overwrite the browser owner's preferences and no test would notice.

samples.summary: No test covers the `shared-document` → `SharedNotesLayout` wiring, including the newly passed `token`
samples.evidence: The uploader test in shared-notes-layout.test.tsx passes `token="tok-1"` directly to the component, so it proves nothing about `<SharedNotesLayout resolved={resolved} token={token} />` in shared-document.tsx. If `token` were undefined/wrong at that call site, image upload behind a share link would silently fall back to `undefined` and the suite stays green. I found no shared-document test file exercising the note branch.

samples.summary: `NotesView` is fully mocked, so prop-level assertions are wiring-only
samples.evidence: The `vi.mock("@/app/notes/notes-view")` stub records props and returns a div. This is reasonable (the real view mounts CodeMirror against a live Yorkie doc) and the layout under test really is wiring, but it means assertions like `viewProps.current.readOnly === true` or `viewMode === 'edit'` never prove the view honors them — that half rests entirely on packages/notes' editor tests. Noting for the record, not as a blocker.
